group.name: Cisco Nexus Controller Receiver
group.description: Dashboard group for API-first Nexus Dashboard, NDFC, Insights, Orchestrator, Data Broker, and Cisco ACI/APIC metrics emitted by the Cisco OS receiver.

variables.description: Nexus or ACI switch serial number.

dashboards.name: 00 Controller API Trust And Coverage
dashboards.description: Value: proves whether Nexus Dashboard and APIC API polling is trustworthy before operators interpret fabric or tenant symptoms.
dashboards.value: Use this page first when API data is missing, stale, or partially successful. It separates controller API health from network impact.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains API trust and service coverage. Interpretation: partial success, unavailable services, or API errors mean downstream fabric charts may be incomplete.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Start here for API-first Nexus troubleshooting. Confirm controller reachability, API latency, partial scrape state, app availability, and object-family coverage before treating downstream fabric or tenant gaps as real network symptoms.

charts.name: Nexus Dashboard API Errors
charts.description: Value: surfaces Nexus Dashboard API failures. Interpretation: non-zero values by operation explain missing NDFC, Insights, NDO, or Data Broker data.

charts.name: Nexus Dashboard API Duration
charts.description: Value: tracks Nexus Dashboard API request latency by operation. Interpretation: high duration without errors points to slow controller/app responses that can make incident data appear stale.

charts.name: Nexus Dashboard Partial Scrape
charts.description: Value: shows whether one or more endpoint families failed or were skipped. Interpretation: 1 means controller coverage is incomplete.

charts.name: Unavailable Nexus Dashboard Services
charts.description: Value: shows ND app/API endpoints that are unavailable, unauthorized, disabled, or not installed. Interpretation: validate installed services and permissions.

charts.name: Nexus Dashboard Endpoint Failures And Skips
charts.description: Value: identifies failed or intentionally skipped ND/NDFC/Insights/NDO/Data Broker endpoint families. Interpretation: use this to separate missing permissions or uninstalled apps from healthy empty results.

charts.name: APIC API Errors
charts.description: Value: surfaces APIC API failures. Interpretation: non-zero values by controller and operation explain missing ACI class data.

charts.name: APIC API Duration
charts.description: Value: tracks APIC API request latency. Interpretation: rising duration with low error count points to controller pressure or slow class queries before data loss.

charts.name: APIC Endpoint Errors And Rate Limits
charts.description: Value: shows APIC class-query failures and API rate-limit evidence. Interpretation: non-zero values explain missing fabric, tenant, endpoint, or topology objects.

charts.name: APIC Partial Scrape
charts.description: Value: shows whether one or more APIC class-query families failed. Interpretation: 1 means ACI coverage is incomplete.

charts.name: APIC Controller Availability
charts.description: Value: shows whether each configured APIC was reachable for the scrape. Interpretation: 0 means the controller API path is unavailable.

charts.name: Collected Object Families
charts.description: Value: proves which controller object families are actually present in telemetry. Interpretation: sudden drops by family indicate API gaps, target filters, or product/service coverage changes.

charts.name: Last Successful Scrape Timestamp
charts.description: Value: exposes the last successful scrape timestamp from each controller path. Interpretation: stale or flat timestamps mean dashboards are looking at old evidence.

charts.name: Nexus Dashboard Rate Limits
charts.description: Value: surfaces Nexus Dashboard API throttling by operation. Interpretation: non-zero rate-limit counts explain stale or missing controller, NDFC, Insights, Orchestrator, or Data Broker panels.

dashboards.name: 01 Nexus Dashboard Platform And NDFC Fabric
dashboards.description: Value: correlates ND platform health, NDFC fabric/switch health, deployment/compliance state, and interface symptoms.
dashboards.value: Use this page when the affected domain is an NDFC-managed Nexus fabric, switch, or interface.

charts.name: Nexus Dashboard Platform Service Health
charts.description: Value: shows ND node, app, feature, license, and storage health. Interpretation: degraded platform services can explain missing NDFC or Insights data before switch symptoms appear.

charts.name: Nexus Dashboard Platform Resource Pressure
charts.description: Value: correlates ND CPU, memory, and storage pressure with API slowness or unavailable services. Interpretation: sustained high utilization points to controller/platform capacity issues.

charts.name: NDFC Fabric Health
charts.description: Value: tracks NDFC fabric, site, or switch health scores. Interpretation: lower scores or degraded statuses identify where to drill in.

charts.name: Nexus Switch Availability From Controller
charts.description: Value: shows switch reachability as reported by NDFC/ND APIs. Interpretation: 0 indicates the controller sees the switch as unavailable or unhealthy.

charts.name: NDFC Deployment Status
charts.description: Value: surfaces policy, image, or change-control deployment state. Interpretation: failed or degraded state is a change-correlation anchor.

charts.name: NDFC Config Compliance
charts.description: Value: tracks NDFC configuration compliance by switch/fabric. Interpretation: falling compliance after a change is a strong candidate for policy drift or failed deployment.

charts.name: NDFC Endpoint And vPC Inventory
charts.description: Value: correlates endpoint scale and vPC peer inventory with switch/fabric health. Interpretation: sudden changes can identify mobility churn, vPC impact, or fabric discovery gaps.

charts.name: NDFC Interface Status
charts.description: Value: shows controller-reported interface status by Nexus switch. Interpretation: down or flapping interfaces near degraded fabrics should be correlated with traffic and deployment state.

charts.name: NDFC Interface Traffic
charts.description: Value: shows controller-reported interface traffic rates. Interpretation: use with interface status and fabric health to identify saturated or silent links.

charts.name: NDFC Resource Status By Family
charts.description: Value: groups NDFC resource status by product group and object type. Interpretation: degraded object families narrow whether the issue is inventory, policy, interface, endpoint, or telemetry sync.

charts.name: Nexus Dashboard Audit And Event Counts
charts.description: Value: counts bounded audit and event evidence from Nexus Dashboard services. Interpretation: spikes in audits, events, anomalies, advisories, alerts, or root causes during an incident point to change or controller-side ownership.

dashboards.name: 02 Insights Root Cause And Advisories
dashboards.description: Value: summarizes Nexus Dashboard Insights anomalies, advisories, scores, and root-cause confidence.
dashboards.value: Use this page during triage and autopsy when Insights has anomaly or root-cause evidence for a fabric, site, switch, or endpoint.

charts.name: Insights Anomaly Count
charts.description: Value: counts active anomalies and advisories by severity/category. Interpretation: prioritize critical and high-confidence evidence.

charts.name: Active Insights Evidence
charts.description: Value: lists currently active anomalies and advisories with affected site/fabric context. Interpretation: start with critical/high severity entries that share a site or fabric with the incident.

charts.name: Insights Score
charts.description: Value: shows Insights health or anomaly scores. Interpretation: falling site/fabric scores narrow the affected domain.

charts.name: Root-Cause Confidence
charts.description: Value: shows root-cause confidence where Insights exposes it. Interpretation: high confidence is stronger evidence during incident reconstruction.

charts.name: Insights Status By Category
charts.description: Value: shows anomaly, advisory, flow, compliance, and recommendation status. Interpretation: unresolved or degraded categories become the incident evidence queue.

charts.name: Insights Resource Status
charts.description: Value: groups Insights resource status by object type and severity. Interpretation: use this when anomaly counts are low but resource health still indicates advisory, flow, or compliance evidence.

dashboards.name: 03 Orchestrator And Data Broker Operations
dashboards.description: Value: tracks multi-site deployment drift and packet-visibility control-plane state.
dashboards.value: Use this page when a network change, multi-site template, or packet-capture visibility path may explain the incident.

charts.name: NDO Deployment Status
charts.description: Value: shows NDO/OneManage deployment, schema, template, and site sync state. Interpretation: failed/degraded state is change evidence.

charts.name: NDO Deployment Count
charts.description: Value: counts NDO/OneManage deployments by site/schema. Interpretation: deployment count changes near an incident establish change timing and blast radius.

charts.name: NDO Policy Deltas
charts.description: Value: tracks policy deltas. Interpretation: non-zero deltas can indicate undeployed or divergent policy.

charts.name: NDO Resource Status
charts.description: Value: groups Orchestrator/OneManage resource health by object type and status. Interpretation: failed schemas, sites, or templates identify where policy is divergent.

charts.name: Data Broker Status
charts.description: Value: shows Data Broker broker, TAP, SPAN, rule, filter, or session state. Interpretation: degraded state can explain missing packet evidence.

charts.name: Data Broker Rule And Session Counts
charts.description: Value: tracks TAP/SPAN/filter/rule/session inventory exposed by Data Broker. Interpretation: sudden drops explain why expected packet evidence is absent.

charts.name: Orchestrator And Data Broker Service Coverage
charts.description: Value: shows unavailable Orchestrator/OneManage and Data Broker endpoints. Interpretation: use this before assuming policy or packet-visibility objects are truly absent.

dashboards.name: 04 ACI Fabric Tenant Endpoint Impact
dashboards.description: Value: correlates APIC fabric health, active faults, tenant policy, endpoint presence, interface state, and topology.
dashboards.value: Use this page when the affected domain is an ACI fabric, tenant, EPG, L3Out, or workload endpoint.

charts.name: ACI Node Availability
charts.description: Value: shows APIC-reported leaf, spine, and controller availability. Interpretation: 0 on an affected node is immediate fabric impact, not just an API visibility issue.

charts.name: ACI Node Resource Pressure
charts.description: Value: correlates APIC-reported CPU and memory pressure with faults, endpoint churn, and interface symptoms. Interpretation: sustained high values can explain delayed control-plane convergence.

charts.name: ACI Active Faults
charts.description: Value: summarizes active APIC faults. Interpretation: critical and major faults by code/domain usually explain the fastest path to root cause.

charts.name: ACI Active Fault Detail
charts.description: Value: lists active faults with affected host and code context. Interpretation: sort by critical/major severity and correlate the host with node, interface, tenant, and topology panels.

charts.name: ACI Fabric Health
charts.description: Value: tracks APIC-reported fabric, pod, node, or tenant health. Interpretation: lower scores narrow the impacted domain.

charts.name: ACI Tenant And Policy Status
charts.description: Value: shows tenant, VRF, bridge-domain, EPG, app profile, contract, and L3Out inventory/status. Interpretation: object-count changes or degraded statuses explain workload impact.

charts.name: ACI Resource Inventory By Domain
charts.description: Value: tracks APIC object inventory by collection group, class, status, and severity. Interpretation: changes show whether the incident aligns with faults, tenants, endpoints, topology, or stats visibility.

charts.name: ACI Endpoint Count
charts.description: Value: tracks endpoint presence by tenant and EPG. Interpretation: sudden drops or churn can identify workload impact.

charts.name: ACI Endpoint Detail
charts.description: Value: lists observed endpoint MAC/IP/DN records within receiver caps. Interpretation: use this to confirm whether a specific workload endpoint is still learned and where it appears in APIC.

charts.name: ACI Interface Status
charts.description: Value: shows APIC interface status. Interpretation: down interfaces near affected endpoints should be investigated with faults and topology.

charts.name: ACI Interface Traffic And Drops
charts.description: Value: correlates optional APIC interface traffic, packet, and drop-rate counters. Interpretation: traffic silence, packet spikes, or drops near affected nodes explain workload impact.
charts.signalflow: data('cisco.interface.io.rate', filter=filter('cisco.controller.type', 'apic')).mean(by=['host.name', 'network.interface.name', 'network.io.direction']).publish(label='Interface rate'); data('cisco.interface.packet.rate', filter=filter('cisco.controller.type', 'apic')).mean(by=['host.name', 'network.interface.name', 'network.io.direction']).publish(label='Packets/sec'); data('cisco.interface.drop.rate', filter=filter('cisco.controller.type', 'apic')).mean(by=['host.name', 'network.interface.name', 'network.io.direction']).publish(label='Drops')

charts.name: ACI Topology Neighbors
charts.description: Value: shows APIC-discovered LLDP/CDP/topology neighbors by local node/interface. Interpretation: missing or changed neighbors identify the physical or logical path tied to endpoint impact.

charts.name: ACI Resource Status
charts.description: Value: shows encoded APIC object status across fabric, faults, endpoints, tenants, and topology. Interpretation: unhealthy rows identify the APIC object family and severity behind user or application impact.

charts.name: ACI Audit And Event Counts
charts.description: Value: counts recent APIC audit and event records with bounded labels. Interpretation: audit or event spikes near a fault window provide change evidence without high-cardinality messages or usernames in metrics.
